          "statement": "Let $N,d\\ge1$ be positive integers, let $f_i:\\mathbb R^d\\to\\mathbb R$\nbe differentiable, and put $f=N^{-1}\\sum_{i=1}^N f_i$. These conditions bound the population\nsecond moment of deterministic client gradients.           "statement": "Let $N,d\\ge1$ be positive integers, let $f_i:\\mathbb R^d\\to\\mathbb R$\nbe differentiable, and put $f=N^{-1}\\sum_{i=1}^N f_i$. For constants\n$G\\ge0$ and $B\\ge1$, the clients have standard $(G,B)$-bounded gradient\ndissimilarity if\n$$ \\frac1N\\sum_{i=1}^N\\|\\nabla f_i(x)\\|_2^2\\le G^2+B^2\\|\\nabla f(x)\\|_2^2 \\qquad(x\\in\\mathbb R^d). $$\n\nFor $\\beta>0$ and a finite global lower bound $f^\\star\\in\\mathbb R$ for\n$f$, the gap-form condition with parameters $(G,B,\\beta,f^\\star)$ is\n$$ \\frac1N\\sum_{i=1}^N\\|\\nabla f_i(x)\\|_2^2\\le G^2+2\\beta B^2(f(x)-f^\\star) \\qquad(x\\in\\mathbb R^d). $$\nIn the convex-client FedAvg results, $\\beta$ is a common gradient Lipschitz\nconstant and $f^\\star$ is the attained minimum of $f$; this is the relaxed\nconvex form of the source's assumption. These conditions bound the population\nsecond moment of deterministic client gradients. They are separate from the\nwithin-client stochastic-gradient noise bound\n$\\mathbb E\\|g_i(x)-\\nabla f_i(x)\\|_2^2\\le\\sigma^2$.",

          "statement": "Let $X,U$ be real Banach spaces, and let continuous maps $H,H_n:X\\to U$ satisfy $\\sup_{a\\in K}\\|H_n(a)-H(a)\\|_U\\to0$ for every norm-compact $K\\subset X$. Then\n$$G_n(a)=H_n(J_n(S_n(a)))$$\nis a finite-sampling family in the displayed definition, with $F_n=E_n$, finite map the identity and output reconstruction $R_n=H_n\\circ J_n:E_n\\to U$, and $G_n\\to H$ uniformly on every norm-compact input set in the actual $U$ norm.\n\nFor the supremum-norm continuous-input case these reconstruction hypotheses always hold with exactly the prescribed tags of arbitrary finite partitions of a nonempty bounded open $D\\subset\\mathbb R^d$ whose maximal cell diameters $h_n$ tend to zero. This reconstructs every input exactly. In both branches $\\|J_nS_n\\|_{X\\to X}\\le1$, and the reconstruction error is bounded by the input modulus of continuity at $2h_n$, uniformly on every compact input family. In a stronger Banach input norm the first clause applies whenever the stated reconstructions converge in that norm; convergence in the supremum norm alone is not substituted for that condition.\n\nA further case needs no input reconstruction. Suppose a raw finite architecture first uses its input only through the sampled pointwise lift in the integral-only field $v_{1,n}(x)=\\sum_j\\omega_{n,j}\\kappa_n(x,\\xi_{n,j})P(a(\\xi_{n,j}))+b_n(x)$, and every later stage acts on this field and the fixed parameters without further access to the original input. Assume these stages are defined and continuous on the compatible Banach spaces in question. Then each raw map itself factors through the finite input sample vector.           "statement": "Let $d\\ge1$, let $U\\subset\\mathbb R^d$ be bounded and open, and let $f:\\overline U\\to\\mathbb R^d$ be continuous.           "title": "Exp4 updates are well-defined, including zero-probability actions",
          "deps": [
            "alg-exp4",
            "def-contextual-bandit-protocol",
            "def-real-exponential-function-and-e",
            "cor-exponential-reciprocal-and-positivity",
            "lem-of-inverse-positive",
            "lem-of-sign-rules",
            "thm-induction-principle"
          ],
          "dependency_level": 5,
          "statement": "For the exact-real Exp4 procedure, take any integers $n\\ge1$, $k>1$, $M>1$, any finite real learning rate $\\eta>0$, and every oblivious reward/advice instance and supplied measurable draws in its input scope. At every round $t\\in[n]$, the expert vector $Q_t$ is a probability vector with strictly positive entries, the action mixture $P_t$ belongs to $\\Delta_k$, and $P_{t,i}=0$ implies $E(t)_{m,i}=0$ for every expert $m$. Every action and expert reward estimate is finite; the corresponding estimated losses $1-\\widehat X_{t,i}$ and $1-\\widetilde X_{t,m}$ are nonnegative. The normalizing denominator is finite and strictly positive, so $Q_{t+1}$ again has strictly positive entries summing to one. The procedure completes its $n$ prescribed rounds and returns all specified outputs.\n\nThe zero-quotient convention is retained exactly. These conclusions do not require positive sampling probability for every action, a uniform exploration mixture, a bound on the magnitude of an importance-weighted estimate, or a restriction on the learning rate beyond $\\eta>0$."
